ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle, $BD$ is the median of $\triangle ABC$. Extend $BC$ to $E$ so that $CE=CD$, and connect $DE$. What is the measure of $\angle BDE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle and BD is the median,\\
therefore, $\angle BDC=90^\circ$, $\angle ACB=60^\circ$\\
thus, $\angle ACE=180^\circ-\angle ACB=180^\circ-60^\circ=120^\circ$,\\
since CE=CD,\\
therefore, $\angle CDE=\angle CED=30^\circ$,\\
thus, $\angle BDE=\angle BDC+\angle CDE=90^\circ+30^\circ=\boxed{120^\circ}$

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle, $BD$ is the median of $\triangle ABC$. Extend $BC$ to $E$ so that $CE=CD$, and connect $DE$. What is the measure of $\angle BDE$?

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, A is above, B is at the lower left, B, C, and E are on the same horizontal line, and E is to the right of C, a point on the extension line of BC. D is located on side AC, and BD and DE are connected; at point D, when turning from ray DB to ray DE, ray DC will be passed through, so DC is between DB and DE.

Reasoning: Because △ABC is an equilateral triangle, ∠ACB=60°. Also because BD is the median from B to AC, in an equilateral triangle, the median is also an altitude, so BD ⟂ AC. Since D and C are on AC, ∠BDC=90°.

Because E is on the extension line of BC, and D is on AC, ∠DCE is the exterior angle of ∠ACB, namely ∠DCE=180°−60°=120°. Also it is known that CE=CD, so △CDE is an isosceles triangle, and the base angles are equal: ∠CDE=∠CED=(180°−120°)/2=30°.

From the order of the rays in the figure, ∠BDE=∠BDC+∠CDE=90°+30°=120°.
